_: The Clean Architecture rules IFX is measured by. This file is IN FORCE for everything under
src/: layerguard's check walks up from whatever path it is given looking for layerguard.json,
and from src/Modules it finds this one. It sits in src/ rather than the repository root so it
governs the code it describes and nothing else — the tooling under mcp/ is not part of this
architecture, and a rule file above it would be found by that project's own tests.
Nothing runs this automatically. It is not an analyzer and no build depends on it, so what it
changes is what `check` reports to whoever asks.
D-3 says Domain declares no package at all, so its allow-list is empty. It once named
IFX.BuildingBlocks.Domain, which was dead weight twice over: Domain declares no package, and
BuildingBlocks.Domain is a project the run loads, never a package.
The two Microsoft.Extensions entries end in * because this list is read twice: against the
packages a project declares, where the id is Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions, and
against imported namespaces, where the same package appears as Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.
The wildcard is what lets one entry cover both, and it is the looser of the two readings.
forbiddenPackages names data-access libraries one by one, because the tool has no idea what
a data-access library is. P-2 is only as complete as this list: a driver nobody wrote down
here passes.
allowedReferences encodes D-2 and A-1, and the last two patterns under Application are the
rulebook's own carve-outs, not the rule: 'a ring referencing a project belonging to another
module' and 'a ring referencing a shared host or platform project' are recorded and never
ruled on. A-1 read on its own would refuse all six of those references. They are listed here
so the exemption is visible in the file rather than hidden in the tool. Own-module
Abstractions stays a violation: the deny-list is read first and X-1 still names it.
forbiddenDependencies encodes only half of C-7. 'Never takes a repository itself' is a
constructor parameter and is judged here. 'Reaches a use case through the mediator' is what
a method body does, which nothing here reads. That half is measured by nothing, and
mcp/LayerGuard/COVERAGE.md is where every such gap is listed.
forbiddenDependencyOrigins encodes C-4's testable half: 'never as a concrete class from
Infrastructure'. Its other half, 'takes its dependencies as interfaces declared in Domain',
is a positive claim about every parameter and is not written as a rule here.
severities carries A-2's own level. The rulebook calls A-2 a bend, not a break: an extra
package in Application is infrastructure work in the wrong ring, not a dependency pointing
the wrong way. Every other rule in the rulebook breaks, except X-2, which the tool already
reports as drift.
ruleRefs maps this tool's rule ids onto the rulebook's numbered rules. The mapping is
many-to-many — RING-DIRECTION serves D-1, A-1, P-1 and I-1, which differ only by ring, and
D-1 alone is settled by four ids — so it is stated here rather than worked out again by
whoever reads a report. First match wins: D-1 carries sameModule so it is claimed before
D-2, which takes the rest. notMeasured is what a clean result does NOT prove.
What this rule set does NOT measure is not written out here twice: every ruleRefs entry
carries its own notMeasured, and describe_rules prints the whole table computed. The tool's
own permanent limits — what parsing cannot see at all — are in mcp/LayerGuard/LIMITS.md.

ruleRefs.text: Domain references no other project of its own module.
Domain's only project reference outside its module is IFX.BuildingBlocks.Domain.
Domain declares no package at all.
Application references its own Domain; a reference to its own Presentation or Infrastructure is a violation.
Application's packages are limited to the use-case libraries.
Presentation references its own Application and may reference its own Domain; its own Infrastructure is a violation.
A data-access package in Presentation is a violation.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: only as complete as the list of libraries forbiddenPackages names; a driver nobody wrote down passes

ruleRefs.text: Infrastructure references its own Application and Domain; its own Presentation is a violation.
No ring references its own module's .Abstractions project.
All four ring projects exist in the module, each named for it.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: that each ring project is named for its module; only that one is present

ruleRefs.text: No Domain file names a database library, web framework, mediator or validation library.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: a type named in full in code, with no import line

ruleRefs.text: Every repository interface is declared in Domain.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: a repository interface whose name is outside the convention the rule file states

ruleRefs.text: No Application file names a database context, database library or web framework.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: a type named in full in code, with no import line

ruleRefs.text: Application takes its dependencies as interfaces declared in Domain, never a concrete class from Infrastructure.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: the positive half: that every dependency IS an interface declared in Domain

ruleRefs.text: Every command and query handler is in Application.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: a handler whose name is outside the convention the rule file states
a validator whose name is outside the convention the rule file states

ruleRefs.text: An endpoint reaches a use case through the mediator and never takes a repository itself.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: the positive half: that a use case IS reached through the mediator

ruleRefs.text: An endpoint returns its own response type, never a Domain entity.
ruleRefs.notMeasured: the whole rule; a return type built inside a method body is not read

ruleRefs.text: Every repository class in Infrastructure implements an interface declared in Domain.
